functionDeclarations.name: analyze_multimedia
functionDeclarations.description:
Analyzes images, videos, and audio files using a multimodal model. This tool accepts local file paths, base64 data, or URLs to multimedia content. Supported formats include common image types (PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, BMP), video formats (MP4, MKV, OGG), and audio formats (MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A).

Key capabilities:
• Visual Agent: Operates PC/mobile GUIs, recognizes UI elements, understands functions, can guide through interface interactions
• Visual Coding: Generates Draw.io diagrams, HTML/CSS/JS code from images/videos
• Text Extraction: Reads and extracts all text from images including documents, receipts, screenshots
• Spatial Perception: Judges object positions, viewpoints, occlusions, provides 2D grounding
• Content Analysis: Describes scenes, identifies objects, analyzes actions in videos
• Audio Understanding: Transcribes speech, identifies sounds, analyzes audio content
• Technical Understanding: Interprets charts, diagrams, technical drawings, code screenshots

The model responds based on your specific prompt. Examples: 'Extract all text from this receipt', 'Generate HTML code for this UI design', 'Identify all clickable elements in this screenshot', 'Describe the spatial relationships between objects', 'Transcribe the speech in this audio', 'What sounds are in this recording?'.

prompt.description: The prompt or question to ask about the multimedia content. Be specific about what you want to know. Examples: 'Describe what you see in this image', 'Extract all text from this receipt', 'Generate HTML/CSS code for this UI design', 'Identify all clickable elements and their functions in this screenshot', 'What actions are happening in this video?', 'Create a Draw.io diagram based on this flowchart image', 'Describe the spatial relationships between objects', 'What UI components are visible and how can I interact with them?', 'Transcribe the speech in this audio file', 'What sounds can you hear in this recording?', 'Identify the speakers in this conversation'.

functionDeclarations.name: cron_create
functionDeclarations.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## Sub-minute schedules (optional 6th seconds field)

Prefix a 6th field for seconds — "S M H DoM Mon DoW", e.g. "30 30 14 28 2 *" fires at 2:30:30pm on Feb 28. Sub-minute cadence is allowed ONLY for one-shot tasks (recurring: false); a recurring job must fire at most once per minute and a sub-minute recurring schedule like "*/30 * * * * *" is rejected. 5-field schedules fire at :00 seconds.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30 to spread load:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it.

## Durability

By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Codely session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Codely exits. Pass durable: true to write to .codely-cli/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts. Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). One-shot tasks fire at exactly their scheduled time. Recurring tasks add a small deterministic forward jitter (up to 10% of their period, max 15 min) to spread load off round wall-clock marks.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to cron_delete.

cron.description: Cron expression in local time. 5-field "M H DoM Mon DoW" (fires at :00 seconds), e.g. "*/5 * * * *" = every 5 minutes, "30 14 28 2 *" = Feb 28 at 2:30pm once. An optional leading 6th field adds seconds: "S M H DoM Mon DoW", e.g. "*/30 * * * * *" = every 30 seconds.

prompt.description: The prompt to enqueue at each fire time.

recurring.description: true (default) = fire on every cron match until deleted or auto-expired after 7 days. false = fire once at the next match, then auto-delete.

durable.description: true = persist to .codely-cli/scheduled_tasks.json and survive restarts. false (default) = in-memory only, dies when this Codely session ends.

actionType.description: Dispatch mode. 'prompt' (default) enqueues the prompt to the model; 'hook' triggers a configured runtime hook. When set to 'hook', hookConfig is REQUIRED. Omit hookConfig entirely for 'prompt'.

hookConfig.description: Hook configuration. REQUIRED when actionType is 'hook'; MUST be omitted otherwise. Only runtime hooks are supported; command hooks are rejected for safety. When type is 'runtime', `hookName` is required.

type.description: 'runtime' triggers a named runtime hook registered for Notification (requires `hookName`).

hookName.description: Runtime hook name to trigger. Required when type is 'runtime'.

functionDeclarations.name: job_create
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the job and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool
Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:
- Complex multi-step tasks - When a job requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Work that requires careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a job list to track the work
- User explicitly requests job list - When the user directly asks you to use the job list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as jobs
- When you start working on a job - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a job - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up jobs discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool
Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward job
- The job is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The job can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The job is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial job to do. In this case you are better off just doing the job directly.

## Job Fields
- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: Detailed description of what needs to be done, including context and acceptance criteria
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when job is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). This is displayed to the user while you work on the job.

**IMPORTANT**: Always provide activeForm when creating jobs. The subject should be imperative ("Run tests") while activeForm should be present continuous ("Running tests"). All jobs are created with status `pending`.

## Tips
- Create jobs with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- Include enough detail in the description for another agent to understand and complete the job
- After creating jobs, use job_update to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check job_list first to avoid creating duplicate jobs
- Use `allowDuplicate: true` only when you intentionally need a second open job with the same normalized subject

subject.description: A brief title for the job

description.description: A detailed description of what needs to be done

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the job

allowDuplicate.description: Set to true to force creation even if a duplicate open job already exists

functionDeclarations.name: job_get
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to retrieve a job by its ID from the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
- When you need the full description and context before starting work on a job
- To understand job dependencies (what it blocks, what blocks it)
- After being assigned a job, to get complete requirements

## Output
Returns full job details:
- **subject**: Job title
- **description**: Detailed requirements and context
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'failed', or 'completed'
- **blocks**: Jobs waiting on this one to complete
- **blockedBy**: Jobs that must complete before this one can start

## Tips
- After fetching a job, verify its blockedBy list is empty before beginning work.
- Use job_list to see all jobs in summary form.

jobId.description: The ID of the job to retrieve

functionDeclarations.name: job_list
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to list all jobs in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
- To see what jobs are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find jobs that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a job, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available job
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones

## Continuation Workflow

- After completing your current job, call job_list to find available work
- Look first for jobs with status 'pending', no owner, and empty blockedBy
- If multiple jobs are available, prefer the lowest-ID job first
- If no jobs are available, remaining work is either completed or blocked and should be handled explicitly

## Output
Returns a summary of each job:
- **id**: Job identifier (use with job_get, job_update)
- **subject**: Brief description of the job
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'failed', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Current execution owner identifier if assigned (auto-linked task execution uses task IDs like `task-1`), empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open job IDs that must be resolved first (jobs with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use job_get with a specific job ID to view full details including description and comments.

functionDeclarations.name: job_update
functionDeclarations.description:
Use this tool to update a job in the job list.

## When to Use This Tool
**Mark jobs as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a job
- When a job is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned jobs as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call job_list to find your next job
- After completing your current job, look for the next available job instead of stopping
- Available jobs are typically: status = 'pending', no owner, and no open blockedBy dependencies
- **Prefer working on jobs in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple jobs are available, as earlier jobs often set up context for later ones
- ONLY mark a job as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the job as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new job describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a job as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete jobs:**
- When a job is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the job

**Update job details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between jobs

## Fields You Can Update
- **status**: The job status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the job title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the job description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the job owner identifier. When a job is auto-linked to a `task`, this is typically the execution task ID (e.g. `task-1`).
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the job (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark jobs that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark jobs that must complete before this one can start
- **removeBlocks**: Remove jobs from this job's blocks list
- **removeBlockedBy**: Remove jobs from this job's blocked-by list

## Status Workflow
Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`
A job can also move to `failed` when a linked task fails, then back to `in_progress` for retry.
Use `deleted` to permanently remove a job.

## Staleness
Make sure to read a job's latest state using `job_get` before updating it.

## Continuation

- After marking a job completed, use `job_list` to check for newly unblocked work
- If a clear unblocked job exists, continue with it rather than pausing for an unnecessary decision
- If no job is available, or remaining work is genuinely blocked or ambiguous, then ask the user or update dependencies accordingly

## Examples
Mark job as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```
Mark job as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```
Delete a job:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```
Claim a job by setting owner:
```json
{"jobId": "1", "owner": "task-1"}
```
Set up job dependencies:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```
Remove a dependency after recovering:
```json
{"jobId": "2", "removeBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

jobId.description: The ID of the job to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Job IDs that this job blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Job IDs that block this job

removeBlocks.description: Job IDs to remove from this job's blocks list

removeBlockedBy.description: Job IDs to remove from this job's blocked-by list

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the job. Set a key to null to delete it.

functionDeclarations.name: replace
functionDeclarations.description:
Replaces text within a file. Use this tool for targeted edits to existing files.

The tool replaces exactly ONE occurrence of `old_string` with `new_string` by default. The `old_string` MUST uniquely identify the specific instance to change — unless `replace_all` is set to true, in which case every occurrence of `old_string` will be replaced. Use the read_file tool to establish the current file state before the first text replacement. If the tool reports that the file changed since it was read, re-read it before retrying.

If you need to replace the full contents of an existing file, use `write_file` instead.
If `old_string` is empty, the tool treats the operation as creating a new file. This is only valid when the target file does not already exist.
Do not use an empty `old_string` to overwrite an existing file.

The user has the ability to modify the `new_string` content. If modified, this will be stated in the response.

Expectation for required parameters:
1. `file_path` MUST be an absolute path; otherwise an error will be thrown.
2. Prefer exact literal text for `old_string`, including relevant surrounding context and matching whitespace, indentation, and newlines when possible.
3. Prefer exact literal text for `new_string`, and ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.
4. NEVER escape `old_string` or `new_string`, that would break the exact literal text requirement.

**Important:** Exact literal matches are the most reliable. The tool may also apply limited deterministic normalization for whitespace, indentation, and escaping, but do not rely on fallback matching when you can provide the exact text. The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify. Must start with '/'.

old_string.description: Prefer exact literal text when possible, preferably unescaped. Include at least 3 lines of context BEFORE and AFTER the target text, matching whitespace and indentation as closely as you can. The `old_string` should uniquely match one location in the file unless `replace_all` is true. Exact matches are the most reliable, and the tool may also apply limited deterministic normalization for whitespace, indentation, and escaping when needed. If `old_string` is empty, the tool treats the operation as creating a new file. This is only valid when the target file does not already exist.

new_string.description: Prefer exact literal text to replace `old_string` with, preferably unescaped. Provide the intended final text and ensure the resulting code is correct and idiomatic.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false). Use this for replacing and renaming strings across the file.

functionDeclarations.name: run_shell_command
functionDeclarations.description:
This tool executes a given shell command using the best available Windows shell (PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt).

IMPORTANT:
- This tool is for terminal operations (e.g., git / npm / docker / build & test commands).
- DO NOT use this tool for file operations like reading, writing, editing, or searching files. Prefer the dedicated file tools for those actions.
- Quote any file path that contains spaces with double quotes, e.g. `cd "/path with spaces"` or `python "/path with spaces/script.py"`.
- If a command would produce very large output, prefer adding flags/filters (narrow paths, limit counts, request specific fields, machine-readable formats like JSON) to keep output small and unambiguous.
- Very large outputs may be returned as the most recent tail of the output. Earlier content may be truncated from the beginning. If the tool reports a "Full output saved to: <path>", that file contains the full command output. Use the exact path returned by the tool, then prefer searching that file first (grep/rg or platform equivalents) for specific ERROR/WARN/FAIL/SUCCESS markers, then reading small slices (with `read_file` using `offset`/`limit`) or tailing the log file instead of re-running expensive commands.
- Do not append truncating pipelines such as `| tail`, `| Select-Object -Last`, or similar to an expensive first run just to suppress output. Those discard earlier context and force a re-run if you later need omitted lines. Let the tool/log capture the full output, then inspect the saved log file.
- When issuing multiple shell commands in one response, parallelize only when they are truly independent and do not compete for the same files, directories, logs, locks, caches, git state, or ports. If one command depends on another or shared state may race, run them sequentially.

The following information is returned:
- Command: Executed command.
- Directory: Directory where command was executed, or `(root)`.
- Output: Combined command output (stdout/stderr). Can be `(empty)` or an excerpt if very large.
- Error: Error or `(none)` if no error was reported for the subprocess.
- Exit Code: Exit code or `(none)` if terminated by signal.
- Signal: Signal number or `(none)` if no signal was received.

command.description: Exact command to execute using the best available Windows shell (automatically selected from PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt). Quote any file paths containing spaces with double quotes.

description.description: Brief description of the command for the user. Be specific and concise. Ideally a single sentence. Can be up to 3 sentences for clarity. No line breaks.

directory.description: (OPTIONAL) The absolute path of the directory to run the command in. If not provided, the project root directory is used. Must be a directory within the workspace and must already exist.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. Returns immediately with task metadata and an output file path.

functionDeclarations.name: search_file_content
functionDeclarations.description: Searches for a regular expression pattern within the content of files in a specified directory, a specific file, or the current working directory. The search backend is ripgrep, so regex patterns use ripgrep/Rust regex syntax, not JavaScript RegExp syntax. If you need to search literal text that contains regex metacharacters (for example $, {, [, (, or \), set fixed_strings: true or -F: true instead of escaping by hand. Can filter files by a glob pattern when searching directories. By default, returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers; set output_mode to "files_with_matches" for just file paths or "count" for per-file match totals. Each matched line is truncated at 500 characters with a "[line truncated from N chars]" suffix to keep minified or base64 content from blowing up context.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for within file contents. This is interpreted by ripgrep/Rust regex, not JavaScript RegExp; avoid JS-only features such as lookbehind and backreferences. Regex syntax errors are returned by ripgrep. For literal text, especially strings containing regex metacharacters like $, {, [, (, or \, prefer fixed_strings: true or -F: true. When passing JSON args, escape only for JSON once: to match literal ${, use pattern "\\$\\{" (the regex engine sees \$\{), not "\\\\$\\\\{".

path.description: Optional: A literal path relative to the workspace root, or an absolute path to a directory or file to search within. This parameter does not support glob or brace syntax; use a common parent path with the glob parameter instead. If a file path is provided, searches only within that file. If a directory path is provided, searches all files in that directory. If omitted, searches the current working directory.

glob.description: Optional: A glob pattern to filter which files are searched (e.g., '*.js', '*.{ts,tsx}', 'src/**'). Single string only — combine multiple patterns via whitespace/comma separation (e.g. '*.js *.ts', '*.js,*.ts') or brace expansion ('*.{ts,tsx}'). Only applicable when searching directories, ignored for file searches. If omitted, searches all files (respecting potential global ignores).

output_mode.description: Optional: Output format. 'content' (default) returns matching lines with line numbers and optional context; 'files_with_matches' returns only the list of matching file paths; 'count' returns per-file match counts.

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of matches to return to prevent context overflow (default: 250, max: 1000). Values above 1000 are clamped automatically. Use lower values for broad searches, higher for specific searches. Pass 0 for unlimited.

head_limit.description: Optional: Claude Code aligned alias for 'maxResults'. When both are provided, head_limit wins. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Optional: Number of matches to skip before returning results. Use this to continue after a truncated result's next offset.

-A.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -A.

-B.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -B.

-C.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for ripgrep's -C.

context.description: Optional: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Only applies to 'content' output_mode. Alias for -C.

-n.description: Optional: Whether to include line numbers in 'content' output. Defaults to true; set to false to omit them.

-i.description: Optional: Case-insensitive matching. Defaults to false (case-sensitive), matching ripgrep behavior.

fixed_strings.description: Optional: Treat the pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression. Alias for -F.

-F.description: Optional: Treat the pattern as a literal string instead of a regular expression. Alias for fixed_strings.

type.description: Optional: ripgrep file type filter (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. Accepts any alias from `rg --type-list`; the value is forwarded verbatim to ripgrep.

multiline.description: Optional: Enable multiline matching where patterns may span newlines (passes -U and --multiline-dotall to ripgrep). Only meaningful for 'content' output_mode. ^/$ anchors keep line boundaries behavior for portability across search backends.

include_hidden.description: Optional: Whether to descend into dot-prefixed directories (e.g. '.git/', '.codely-cli/') and match dot-prefixed files. Defaults to false to mirror ripgrep's default hidden-skip behaviour. Set to true to scan hidden paths explicitly (passes --hidden to ripgrep).

functionDeclarations.name: send_message_to_task
functionDeclarations.description:
Sends a message to a running task (subagent). The message is injected into the subagent's next model call at a tool-round boundary, alongside any pending tool results.

Fire-and-continue: this tool does NOT block on the subagent response. To observe the subagent's answer, wait for `<bg_task_done>` (background) or the foreground task tool result. To peek at progress, use task_output (subject to allowProgressPeek policy).

Constraints:
- task must exist and be running (no auto-resume of terminal tasks)
- message must be non-empty after trimming
- Excluded from subagent tool registries: subagents cannot themselves call send_message_to_task (avoids nested message storms)

task_id.description: The ID of the running task to send a message to. Use task_output to discover running task ids.

message.description: The message text to inject into the running subagent. The subagent will see it at the next tool-round boundary and address it before completing its current task.

summary.description: Optional short preview of the message (CC SendMessage parity). Used by the TUI as a one-line preview badge.

functionDeclarations.name: task
functionDeclarations.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.

The Task tool launches specialized agents that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each agent has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent names and detailed routing guidance are listed once in the system prompt. Use only those names for subagent_name.

When using the Task tool, you must set the subagent_name parameter to one of the agent names listed in the system prompt.

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- If you want to read a specific file path, use the read_file or glob tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the glob tool instead, to find the match more quickly
- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the read_file tool instead of the Task tool, to find the match more quickly
- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above

Usage notes:
- Always include a short description (3-5 words) summarizing what the agent will do
- Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses
- When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Optional display name: the name parameter is only for UI/tracking display. If omitted, description is used as the display name.
- You can optionally run agents in the background using the run_in_background parameter, but only for genuinely independent work. When an agent runs in the background, you will be notified when it completes.
- Foreground is the default. Use foreground when you need the agent's results before deciding the next step, especially research that informs implementation.
- Use background only when the work is genuinely independent and can safely complete later, such as long-running tests, build validation, independent audits, or non-overlapping research.
- After launching background tasks, do NOT call `task_output` to poll or block — continue with non-overlapping work or respond to the user. Only check progress if the user explicitly asks or the result was truncated.
- Never guess or summarize background task results before the `<bg_task_done ...>...</bg_task_done>` notification arrives.
- Do not duplicate work on the same files or topic as a running background task.
- If this execution corresponds to an existing planned job, pass job_id so the linked job is auto-claimed and auto-updated on completion/failure.
- IMPORTANT: After launching background tasks, do NOT call `task_output` to poll or block — continue with other work or respond to the user. When a background task finishes, a `<bg_task_done task_id="..." name="..." status="...">result</bg_task_done>` message is automatically injected into the conversation containing the task result. Use this directly, and only use `task_output` if the result was truncated or you need additional details.
- Provide clear, detailed prompts so the agent can work autonomously and return exactly the information you need.
- The agent's outputs should generally be trusted
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Task tool use content blocks.

Example usage:
<example>
user: "Please refactor the authentication module to use JWT"
assistant: First let me explore the existing auth implementation.
assistant: Uses the Task tool with an appropriate subagent_name from the system prompt to search for and understand the current authentication code
assistant: Based on the exploration results, I'll now implement the JWT refactoring.
</example>
<example>
user: "Where is the database connection configured?"
assistant: Uses the Task tool with an appropriate subagent_name from the system prompt to find database configuration files
</example>

name.description: Optional display name for UI/tracking (e.g. "Refactor login module"). If omitted, description is used as the display name.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The full task instructions for the agent to perform.

subagent_name.description: The agent to use for this task. Must be one of the available agent names listed in the system prompt.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this agent in the background. You will be notified when it completes with the result.

job_id.description: Optional existing job ID to link this task to. When provided, the linked job is auto-claimed as in_progress and auto-updated on completion/failure.

resume_task_id.description: Optional ID of a terminated task to resume. The new task replays the original task conversation and continues from there, inheriting its linked job when job_id is omitted. Use for tasks that stopped without completing after a crash. Do not use for user-aborted tasks — dispatch a fresh task instead. If resume fails (missing/corrupted transcript), dispatch a fresh task instead.

functionDeclarations.name: task_output
functionDeclarations.description:
Retrieves output for one or more tasks (always non-blocking).
- Use task_id for a single task, or task_ids[] for batch query
- For running tasks: returns stable metadata (status/name/output_file)
- For terminal tasks: includes parsed result summary and complete_task args (when available)
- IMPORTANT: This tool returns immediately with a status snapshot. Do NOT use it to poll or wait for task completion. Rely on <bg_task_done> events instead.

parametersJsonSchema.description: Provide either task_id (single) or task_ids (batch), not both.

task_id.description: A single task ID to query. Required if task_ids is not provided.

task_ids.description: Batch query: multiple task IDs. Required if task_id is not provided. Mutually exclusive with task_id.

functionDeclarations.name: task_stop
functionDeclarations.description:
Stops a running background task by its ID.
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- Returns a success or failure status

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop.

functionDeclarations.name: unity_asset
functionDeclarations.description:
Manage Unity project assets on disk (under "Assets/") such as materials, physics materials, textures/importers, ScriptableObjects, and existing prefabs.

Key uses:
- Read: search assets, get info (optionally with preview), get components from a Prefab asset
- Write: create folders/materials/physics materials/scriptable objects; modify existing assets (including setting Prefab component properties); move/rename/duplicate assets; ensure .meta health

Important notes:
- `create` currently supports only: Folder, Material, PhysicsMaterial, ScriptableObject (Prefab creation is not supported).
- `rename` is effectively a move: pass a full destination asset path (e.g. "Assets/Foo/NewName.ext").
- `generate_preview` can return large base64 payloads; avoid unless you truly need a thumbnail.

Asset (re)import operations are heavy and should only be used when absolutely necessary. Prefer normal Unity import, ensure_*, and script recompilation instead of full reimport.

action.description:
Operation to perform.

Notes:
- `ensure_has_meta` verifies a .meta exists (generates via safe reimport if missing).
- `ensure_meta_integrity` checks meta health and returns recommendations (no auto-fix).
- `rename` behaves like `move` (destination is a full asset path, not just a name).
- `create` supports only: Folder, Material, PhysicsMaterial, ScriptableObject.
- `modify` can edit Prefab assets by setting component properties (see `properties`).

mode.description: Batch mode: 'stop_on_error' stops at first failure (default). 'continue_on_error' runs all ops and collects failures.

ops.description: Batch operations (server-side). Each op runs sequentially inside Unity. Constraints: max 10 ops. Use create_batch for write-only sequences (no reads). Use edit_batch for "search-then-write" edits: one or more search ops with captureAs (must match <= 1 asset; 0 matches => early-stop success), followed by write ops that use the captured $alias as their path.

params.description: Parameters for the op action (same shape as unity_asset, minus action).

allowFailure.description: If true, this op failure won't stop execution even in stop_on_error mode.

captureAs.description: edit_batch only: for search ops, capture the resolved asset path into a $alias (e.g. '$asset') for later write ops.

path.description:
Asset path or scope.
- For most actions, pass a Unity asset path under `Assets/` (e.g. "Assets/Materials/MyMaterial.mat").
- For `search`, `path` is treated as a folder scope (e.g. "Assets/" or "Assets/MyFolder").
- For batch actions, paths are typically provided per-op in `ops[].params.path`.

asset_type.description:
Asset type (e.g., 'Material', 'Folder') - required for `create`.
NOTE: `create` currently supports only: Folder, Material, PhysicsMaterial, ScriptableObject.

assetType.description: Alias of asset_type (camelCase). Prefer this in prompts; will be sent as asset_type to Unity.

properties.description:
Dictionary of properties for "create" "modify".
example properties for Material: {"color": [1, 0, 0, 1], "shader": "Standard"}.
example Material texture assignment: {"texture": {"name": "_MainTex", "path": "Assets/Textures/T.png"}}.
example properties for Texture: {"width": 1024, "height": 1024, "format": "RGBA32"}.
example properties for PhysicsMaterial: {"bounciness": 1.0, "staticFriction": 0.5, "dynamicFriction": 0.5}.
example Prefab component modification (Prefab asset only): {"MyComponent": {"someField": 123, "enabled": true}}.
Tip: when setting UnityEngine.Object fields (e.g., Texture, Material), pass an asset path string; Unity will load and assign it.

shader.description: Shader name for materials (e.g., "Standard", "Universal Render Pipeline/Lit")

color.description: RGBA color values [r, g, b, a] where each component is 0-1

frictionCombine.description: How friction values are combined in physics materials

bounceCombine.description: How bounce values are combined in physics materials

scriptClass.description: Class name for ScriptableObject creation (required for ScriptableObject type)

destination.description: Destination asset path under "Assets/" for duplicate/move/rename (rename is a move to the new path). Example: "Assets/NewFolder/NewName.mat".

generate_preview.description: Generate preview for the asset (may include large base64 PNG). Use sparingly.

filter_type.description: Filter by asset type for search operations

functionDeclarations.name: unity_bake
functionDeclarations.description: Handles NavMesh and Lighting baking operations. Supports async operation tracking for long-running bake processes with configurable timeouts. Can also clear baked NavMesh and lighting data.

async.description: For bake_navmesh: use async UpdateNavMesh instead of synchronous BuildNavMesh. Requires existing NavMesh data on surfaces.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for the operation (default: 600)

functionDeclarations.name: unity_console
functionDeclarations.description: Gets messages from or clears the Unity Editor console. Supports filtering by message type, text content, and formatting options. There are no incremental reads: clear the console to establish a boundary, then read it.

scope.description: Scope for clear action: "all" clears everything (default), "errors_only" clears only error messages

count.description: Maximum number of messages to return

filterText.description: Text filter for messages (case-insensitive substring match)

sinceTimestamp.description: (DEPRECATED) Ignored by Unity. Incremental reads no longer exist: clear the console to establish a boundary, then read.

functionDeclarations.name: unity_dialog
functionDeclarations.description: Clicks a button on a native modal dialog that is blocking the Unity editor main thread. Handled on a background thread in the editor, so it works while the dialog has the editor frozen. When such a dialog appears, in-flight jobs are detached with a reason listing the dialog title/message/buttons — choose a button (param "button" is a regex over the button labels, optional "title" filters by dialog title), click it with this tool, then use unity_job (action "status") to collect the detached jobs' results.

button.description: Regex matched against the dialog button labels; the first matching button is clicked

title.description: Optional regex matched against dialog titles to pick which dialog to click

functionDeclarations.name: unity_editor
functionDeclarations.description: Controls Unity Editor state (play/pause/stop), retrieves project information and full UnityCurrentState, manages editor tools, windows, selection, tags, and layers. Use get_state for a comprehensive state snapshot.

action.description: Action to perform. Use "get_state" for full state (alias: get_current_state), "start_compilation_pipeline" after script changes (alias: request_compile), "wait_for_idle" to wait until every in-flight bridge job has finished and the editor is neither compiling nor importing, "focus_window" to focus a specific editor window. Every action returns only once it has finished — compilation and play/pause/stop block until the editor has actually reached the requested state, so there is no wait_for_compile / wait_for_stop.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for the operation (default: 300 for compile, 600 for wait_for_idle, 120 for play mode)

clearCache.description: For start_compilation_pipeline: clear the script assembly cache (Library/ScriptAssemblies) before compiling (default: false)

waitForCompletion.description: Wait for action to complete before returning

tagName.description: Tag name for add_tag or remove_tag actions

layerName.description: Layer name for add_layer or remove_layer actions

windowType.description: Window type for focus_window action. Common types: Console, Inspector, Hierarchy, Project, Scene, Game, Animator, Animation, Profiler

functionDeclarations.name: unity_gameobject
functionDeclarations.description: Manages Unity GameObjects with comprehensive operations including create, modify, delete, find, list_children, and component management. Supports primitives, prefabs, transforms, and advanced component manipulation with property setting and reference assignments.

action.description: Operation to perform. Ensure operations are idempotent (safe to call multiple times). `set_component_properties` is an alias of `set_component_property` (recommended for batch property sets). Use `create_batch` for write-only deterministic batches (no reads); use `edit_batch` for "find-then-write" edits with an early-stop when 0 targets are found. Use "list_children" to retrieve a depth-limited *tree-structured* children hierarchy for a specific GameObject (large results can be written to a JSON file under Assets/). Use "select" to set Unity Editor selection. For full-scene hierarchy roots, prefer unity_scene action="get_hierarchy".

mode.description: Batch mode: 'stop_on_error' stops at first failure (default). 'continue_on_error' runs all ops and collects failures.

ops.description: Batch operations (server-side). Each op runs sequentially inside Unity. Constraints: max 10 ops. Use create_batch for write-only sequences (no reads). Use edit_batch for "find-then-write" edits: one or more find ops with captureAs (must match <= 1 target; 0 matches => early-stop success), followed by write ops that target the captured $alias (no by_name targeting in write phase).

params.description: Parameters for the op action (same shape as unity_gameobject, minus action).

allowFailure.description: If true, this op failure won't stop execution even in stop_on_error mode.

captureAs.description: Optional alias (e.g. '$root') to bind this op's primary GameObject instanceID (typically from create) for later refs.

component_type.description: Component type name for ensure_component action

componentType.description: Alias of component_type (camelCase). Prefer this in prompts; will be sent as component_type to Unity.

material.description: Material asset path or GUID for ensure_renderer_material action

mesh.description: Mesh asset path or GUID for ensure_mesh_collider_mesh action

prefab.description: Prefab asset path or GUID for ensure_prefab_default_sprite action

sprite.description: Sprite asset path or GUID for ensure_prefab_default_sprite action

target.description: GameObject identifier (name/path/instance ID) for modify/delete/component actions. Prefer `targetRef` for structured targeting. For list_children, this is the root GameObject whose subtree will be returned.

targetRef.description: Preferred structured reference for the target GameObject. If provided, the tool will derive target+searchMethod. Fields: { id?: number, name?: string, hierarchy_path?: string }.

searchMethod.description: How to find objects. "by_name" (default): match GameObject name. "by_id": match instance ID. "by_path": match hierarchy path (e.g. "Parent/Child"). "by_tag": find by Unity tag. "by_layer": find by layer name or index. "by_component": find objects with specific component type.

name.description: GameObject name - used for both "create" (initial name) and "modify" (rename)

tag.description: Tag name - used for both "create" (initial tag) and "modify" (change tag)

parent.description: Parent GameObject reference - used for both "create" (initial parent) and "modify" (change parent)

rotation.description: Rotation as [x, y, z] Euler angles

componentsToAdd.description: List of component names to add

saveAsPrefab.description: Save the created GameObject as a prefab

prefabFolder.description: Folder for prefab if path not specified

layer.description: Layer name - used for both "create" (initial layer) and "modify" (change layer)

componentsToRemove.description: List of component names to remove

componentProperties.description: Dict mapping Component names to their properties to set. Example: {"Rigidbody": {"mass": 10.0, "useGravity": true}}. To set references: Use asset path string for Prefabs/Materials, e.g., {"MeshRenderer": {"material": "Assets/Materials/MyMat.mat"}}. Use a dict for scene objects/components, e.g.: {"MyScript": {"otherObject": {"find": "Player", "method": "by_name"}}} (assigns GameObject), {"MyScript": {"playerHealth": {"find": "Player", "component": "HealthComponent"}}} (assigns Component). Example set nested property: Access shared material: {"MeshRenderer": {"sharedMaterial.color": [1, 0, 0, 1]}}. For action="set_component_property", you can also pass a *flat* object of properties (e.g. {"mass": 10}) or a nested object under componentName (e.g. {"Rigidbody": {"mass": 10}}).

findAll.description: Find all matching GameObjects (not just first)

depth.description: For list_children action: how many levels below target to traverse (1 = direct children). The returned result keeps a tree structure (nested "children") up to this depth.

includeInactive.description: For list_children action: whether to include inactive objects in the returned results (alias of searchInactive).

resultMode.description: For list_children action: 'auto' returns inline unless the result exceeds maxInlineItems, then writes the full tree JSON to a file and returns its path; 'inline' errors if too large (no truncation); 'file' always writes JSON to disk and returns its path.

maxInlineItems.description: For list_children action: maximum number of descendant nodes (within depth) allowed for inline output before switching to file (or erroring in inline mode).

outputPath.description: For list_children action with resultMode='file' (or auto overflow): output JSON path under Assets/. The tool returns this path so callers can read the full, untruncated result.

selectAll.description: For select action: select all matching GameObjects (not just first). If false, only the first match is selected.

propertyName.description: Shorthand: property name for set_component_property. Alternative: omit propertyName/propertyValue and provide componentProperties (non-empty object) to set multiple properties at once.

propertyValue.description: Shorthand: property value for set_component_property. Alternative: omit propertyName/propertyValue and provide componentProperties (non-empty object) to set multiple properties at once.

includeNonPublicSerialized.description: If True, includes private fields marked [SerializeField] in component data

functionDeclarations.name: unity_gameview
functionDeclarations.description: Gets, sets, and lists the Unity Game View resolution. set_resolution selects an existing fixed resolution or creates one when missing.

action.description: Game View operation: "get_resolution" – return the currently selected resolution; "set_resolution" – select (creating if needed) a fixed width×height resolution; "list_resolutions" – list every resolution in the current size group.

width.description: [set_resolution – REQUIRED] Target width in pixels. Must be between 1 and 8192.

height.description: [set_resolution – REQUIRED] Target height in pixels. Must be between 1 and 8192.

functionDeclarations.name: unity_input
functionDeclarations.description: Simulates mouse and keyboard input in Unity PlayMode across multiple frames. IMPORTANT — before any mouse operation on UI: first call the "unity_screenshot" tool to capture the Game View, then read the target UI element's on-screen position from that screenshot and pass those coordinates here. Do NOT guess UI coordinates; screenshot first so clicks/drags land on the right element. Remember coordinates are Unity screen space (bottom-left origin, Y up), so convert if the screenshot pixels are top-left origin. Mouse actions (click, down, up, drag, scroll, and move-hover) dispatch Unity EventSystem UI events when a UI element is hit — the reliable path for UI automation (buttons, sliders, scroll views, toggles, drag-drop). When no UI is hit they fall back to virtual-device injection for world/gameplay input. IMPORTANT: keyboard input and any mouse action over non-UI require calling "create_virtual_devices" first (they error out otherwise); call "destroy_virtual_devices" when done (also auto-restored on play-mode exit). UI interactions that hit a UI element do NOT need the virtual devices. All coordinates use Unity screen space: bottom-left origin, Y increases upward (0,0 = bottom-left).  Use "type_text" to enter a string into a focused uGUI/TMP input field (click the field first); it needs no virtual devices. Use "sequence" to chain multiple input actions in a single call with configurable frame delays between steps. A typical gameplay run: create_virtual_devices -> input actions -> destroy_virtual_devices. Device keyboard actions require the Input System package (com.unity.inputsystem) with Active Input Handling set to "Input System Package (New)" or "Both" in Player Settings.

action.description: Input action to perform. "mouse_click" – click at (x, y); dispatches a uGUI click on a UI hit, else needs virtual devices. "mouse_move" – update UI hover (enter/exit); moving the game cursor over non-UI needs virtual devices. "mouse_drag" – drag from (from_x, from_y) to (x, y); uGUI drag on a UI hit, else needs virtual devices. "mouse_scroll" – scroll at (x, y); UI scroll on a hit, else needs virtual devices. "mouse_down" – press and hold at (x, y): presses the hit UI element (held until mouse_up), else needs virtual devices. "mouse_up" – release the held press; fires a click if press and release land on the same UI element. "key_press" – tap a key (press then release across frames). Needs virtual devices; but with a UI input field focused, editing keys (Backspace, Enter, arrows, …) go to that field and need no devices. "key_down" – hold a key until key_up. Needs virtual devices. "key_up" – release a held key. Needs virtual devices. "type_text" – type a string into the focused uGUI/TMP input field (focus it first via mouse_click). Needs no virtual devices. "create_virtual_devices" – create the virtual mouse/keyboard for gameplay input (disables real devices while active). REQUIRED before device keyboard input or a mouse action over non-UI. "destroy_virtual_devices" – remove the virtual devices and restore the real ones (also happens automatically on play-mode exit). "sequence" – execute an ordered list of steps with configurable delays.

x.description: Target X position in pixels (bottom-left origin, Unity screen space). Used by mouse_click, mouse_move, mouse_drag (destination), mouse_scroll, mouse_down.

y.description: Target Y position in pixels (bottom-left origin, Y increases upward, Unity screen space). Used by mouse_click, mouse_move, mouse_drag (destination), mouse_scroll, mouse_down.

target.description: Forces the path for a positional mouse action (mouse_click/move/drag/scroll/down) instead of hit-testing. "auto" (default): UI when the point is over a UI element, else the virtual device. "ui": EventSystem/uGUI only — errors if nothing is hit, never falls to the device. "world": virtual device only — skips the UI raycast, so it drives gameplay input even under a UI element.

from_x.description: Drag start X position in pixels (bottom-left origin, Unity screen space).

from_y.description: Drag start Y position in pixels (bottom-left origin, Y increases upward, Unity screen space).

drag_speed.description: Drag interpolation speed in pixels per second (default 500, 0 = instant). Higher values complete faster.

scroll_y.description: Vertical scroll amount in pixels (default 0, positive = up).

key.description: Key name using Input System Key enum names. Used by key_press, key_down, key_up. Common values: "W" "A" "S" "D" "Space" "Enter" "Escape" "Tab" "LeftShift" "LeftCtrl" "LeftAlt" "F1"–"F12" "UpArrow" "DownArrow" "LeftArrow" "RightArrow" "Backspace" "Delete". "Return" is accepted as an alias for "Enter". For key_press with a focused input field, editing keys (Backspace/Delete/Enter/Tab/Escape/Home/End/arrows) are sent to the field; use type_text for printable characters.

text.description: Text to type into the focused uGUI/TMP input field, for the "type_text" action. Focus the field first (e.g. mouse_click on it). Needs no virtual devices.

steps.description: Ordered list of input steps for the "sequence" action. Each step is an object with an "action" field (one of the non-sequence actions) plus that action's parameters. A step may include "delay_after" (int, frames) to add extra delay after it completes. Example: [{ "action": "mouse_click", "x": 100, "y": 200 }, { "action": "key_press", "key": "Space", "delay_after": 3 }]

action.description: The input action for this step.

delay_after.description: Extra frames to wait after this step finishes, on top of the global step_delay.

start_delay.description: Frames to wait before the very first step in a sequence (default 0).

step_delay.description: Frames to wait between consecutive steps in a sequence (default 1). Per-step "delay_after" is added on top.

stop_on_error.description: Abort the sequence when a step returns an error (default true).

functionDeclarations.name: unity_job
functionDeclarations.description: Queries in-flight Unity bridge jobs. Handled on a background thread in the Unity editor, so it works even while the main thread is busy or blocked. Actions: status/check (poll a job by id; a finished result is returned exactly once), list (all in-flight jobs). When a response reports a job as detached (e.g. because a modal dialog blocked the editor), use action "status" with the job id to query its state and collect the result.

action.description: Job operation to perform (check is an alias of status)

job_id.description: Job id from a detached/pending response (required for status/check)

functionDeclarations.name: unity_menu

The user asks for a conversation analysis summary. Let me provide a comprehensive summary of everything that was accomplished in this session.

This was a long game development session for a Unity 2D top-down roguelike game (microbial/medical theme). The main work was creating many skills. Let me organize by:

1. Skills created/modified
2. Key architectural enhancements
3. Key bugs/pitfalls discovered
4. Current state

Let me go through the major skills:

1. **轴突传导阻滞 (axon_block)** — 圆形波扩散 + 时停。重制多次：修复波不可见（Sprite 1x1 PPU=1）、画面扭曲覆盖层（0.5s sin 脉冲）、只挡一次等。

2. **溶栓灌注 (thrombolytic_infusion)** — 持续喷射。调试多轮优化液体特效（扫描线→粒子喷溅→调浓）。后取消光效。

3. **高渗裂解剂 (hypertonic_lysate)** — 地面溶液。修复特效不显示（sprite 序列化丢失）、改为挂 debuff（圈内刷新）。

4. **急性谵妄 (acute_delirium)** — 全房间敌人混乱。新增 ConfusedState + DeliriumBuff + DeliriumTrigger。

5. **角质增生覆膜 (keratin_shield)** — 护盾架盾。多次迭代：只挡一次、格挡后无敌帧（DamageImmunity）、圆形硬遮罩防方形。

6. **镇痛阻滞 (analgesic_block)** — 伤害延迟。ApplyBuffSkillEffect 泛用类 + AnalgesicBlockRuntime（延迟池）+ 痛觉残留 DOT + IgnoreStun。

7. **腹膜透析 (peritoneal_dialysis)** — 清除 debuff + 回血。BuffManager.RemoveAllDebuffs + Indestructible 标记（藏品不可清除）。

8. **包膜爆发冲击 (capsular_burst)** — 突进 + 爆发气浪。SlideRuntime 扩展（autoAimNearest + burstOnHit）。多次修复物理乱窜（Kinematic + 禁 collider + transform 位移）、气浪推开（BurstPushComponent）。

9. **肠管蠕动冲击 (intestinal_peristalsis)** — 气浪特效。白色调。

10. **线粒体生物光子辐散 (photon_radiance)** — 天降光柱。SummonSkillEffect 扩展（preferEnemySpawn）+ PhotonBeam。多次迭代：sprite 丢失、2.5D 竖立、从天而降、3 阶段（预警/落下/辐射池）、去掉 8 段改一次性伤害 + 辐射池接续。

Key architectural components:
- ApplyBuffSkillEffect (泛用挂 buff 技能类)
- DamageImmunity (通用无敌组件)
- BurstPushComponent (气浪击退)
- PhotonRadiancePool (辐射池)
- BuffSystem enhancements: RefreshDuration/ExtendDuration/ResetCooldown/RemoveAllDebuffs/Indestructible

Key pitfalls:
1. Sprite.Create 序列化丢失 → sprite=null 不渲染（多次遇到）
2. shader 圆形遮罩参数必须 ≤1（否则 smoothstep 恒 0）
3. 运行时组件挂施法者身上时只能 Destroy(this)
4. 冲刺物理坑（Dynamic 反弹、Kinematic MovePosition 阻塞）
5. OverlapCircleAll 必须用 ~0 mask

Also there was an icon generation credit issue (blocker).

The instructions say "provide the summary as specified" but there's no specific format template provided, so I'll use a clear organized summary.# 会话总结 — WenJianGamejam_2026 技能开发

## 总体成果
本次会话围绕一个 2D 俯视微生物主题 roguelike（Unity 2022.3 URP），**从零开发/重制了 10 个技能**，并沉淀了可复用的泛用技能/ buff 体系。

## 技能清单（全部已注册 SkillLibrary）

| 技能 | 机制 | 关键实现 |
|------|------|---------|
| **轴突传导阻滞** axon_block | 圆形波+时停2s | WaveSkillEffect+WaveRuntime（泛用扩散波）、Sprite 1x1 PPU=1、0.5s sin 脉冲扭曲 |
| **溶栓灌注** thrombolytic_infusion | 持续扇形喷射+后坐力 | TorrentSkillEffect+TorrentRuntime、粒子液滴、移动锁定 InputLocked |
| **高渗裂解剂** hypertonic_lysate | 地面溶液+圈内刷新 debuff | PhotonRadiancePool 前身（GroundSolutionZone 模式，圈内 ApplyBuff+Refresh）|
| **急性谵妄** acute_delirium | 全房间敌人混乱 | ConfusedState + DeliriumBuff + DeliriumTrigger |
| **角质增生覆膜** keratin_shield | 架盾挡一次+完美格挡 | KeratinShieldRuntime、DamageImmunity 无敌帧、AttackLocked/SpeedMultiplier |
| **镇痛阻滞** analgesic_block | 50%伤害延迟 | ApplyBuffSkillEffect（泛用挂buff类）+ AnalgesicBlockRuntime 延迟池 + 痛觉残留 DOT + IgnoreStun |
| **腹膜透析** peritoneal_dialysis | 清 debuff+回血 | BuffManager.RemoveAllDebuffs + Indestructible 标记（藏品不可清除）|
| **包膜爆发冲击** capsular_burst | 自动锁敌突进+气浪 | SlideRuntime 扩展（autoAimNearest/burstOnHit）+ BurstPushComponent |
| **肠管蠕动冲击** intestinal_peristalsis | 白色气浪推开 | 气浪 shader（宽软多环+FBM湍流+swirl）|
| **线粒体生物光子辐散** photon_radiance | 预警+天降光柱+辐射池 | SummonSkillEffect 扩展（preferEnemySpawn 90%）、PhotonBeam 3 阶段、PhotonRadiancePool 接续持续伤害 |

## 泛用体系沉淀（可复用）
- **SkillEffectBase 子类**：Wave/Torrent/Slide/Summon/Projectile/ApplyBuff 6 种泛用效果类，参数驱动可配任意技能
- **Buff 系统增强**：RefreshDuration/ExtendDuration/SetRemainingDuration/ResetCooldown/RemoveAllDebuffs/Indestructible
- **通用组件**：DamageImmunity（无敌帧）、BurstPushComponent（击退）、AnalgesicBlockRuntime（伤害延迟池）、PhotonRadiancePool（辐射池）
- **敌人双向支持**：所有技能通过 ISkillCaster + EnemySkillManager.LoadSkills 敌人可用

## 关键坑（多次踩到并修复）
1. **Sprite.Create 序列化丢失** → `sprite=null` 不渲染（光柱/溶液/护盾都遇到）→ Start 里重建纯白 1x1
2. **shader 圆形遮罩参数必须 ≤1**（UV dist 上限 √2）→ >1 时 smoothstep 恒 0 遮罩失效露方形
3. **运行时组件挂施法者身上** → 只能 `Destroy(this)` 不能 `Destroy(gameObject)`（否则销毁玩家）
4. **冲刺物理坑**：Dynamic MovePosition 反弹 / Kinematic MovePosition 被场景 collider 阻塞 → 最终方案 Kinematic+禁自身 collider+transform 位移
5. **OverlapCircleAll 必须用 `~0` mask**（无 mask 漏检 collider）
6. **2.5D 竖立视觉**：正交相机下 Sprite 旋转无效 → 用"顶部光斑+垂直光束"造型贴图
7. **文件修改后需 `AssetDatabase.Refresh(ForceUpdate)`** 才生效

Use `task` for complex tasks requiring specialized analysis.

- **ai-generation-planner**: Planning agent for MULTI-TASK AI generation requests in Unity. Use only when the user's request involves TWO OR MORE distinct AI generation tasks (e.g. 'generate a character AND a skybox AND a material'). Do NOT use for a single generation task — dispatch the appropriate specialist agent directly instead. Analyzes requirements, decomposes into sub-tasks, resolves dependencies, and produces a structured execution plan.
- **animated-character-generator**: Generates rigged humanoid 3D characters with animations in Unity using Meshy AI, with automatic rotation correction to ensure the character stands upright and faces the camera
- **audio-generator**: Generates background music (BGM) and sound effects (SFX) in Unity using AI, correctly configures AudioSource settings for in-scene playback, and recovers from domain reload by detecting real vs. placeholder audio files
- **effect-video-generator**: Generates effect videos with automatic green-screen keying in Unity. Backend auto-chains gpt-image-2 (with auto green-screen prompt) + seedance2 (green-screen video). Unity auto-creates a ChromaKey material — use with VideoPlayer + RenderTexture for real-time transparent playback. Use for VFX effects like fire, ice, lightning, magic, smoke, particle, energy, explosion effects (特效视频, 绿幕特效, 火焰特效, 魔法特效, 烟雾特效, 粒子特效, 能量特效, 闪电特效, 爆炸特效).
- **explore**: Fast read-only codebase search agent for finding files, patterns, and answering questions about the codebase. Use when you need to quickly find files by patterns, search code for keywords, or understand how parts of the codebase work. Specify thoroughness: 'quick' for basic searches, 'medium' for moderate exploration, 'very thorough' for comprehensive analysis.
- **game-ui-kit-generator**: Generates game UI asset kits in Unity using a two-step AI workflow: Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot from text, Step 2 converts it into a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction. Use for game HUD design, inventory screens, skill bars, menu UI, dialogue boxes — any game UI layout or UI element extraction. (游戏UI, HUD, 界面设计, UI Kit, 背包界面, 技能栏, 主菜单)
- **general-purpose**: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you.
- **image-generator**: Generates image assets (Texture2D PNG) in Unity using AI from text prompts or reference images. Supports Frontier Game Design (default, game-focused), 火山 SeeDream (with segmentation/size options), and Frontier (stylized effects). Use this agent for general-purpose image generation — concept art, UI backgrounds, textures, posters, banners — NOT for game sprites with transparent backgrounds (use sprite-and-sprite-sequence-generator instead).
- **image-upscaler**: Upscales images in Unity using AI super-resolution (Real-ESRGAN). Supports 1x-8x upscaling with model variants for photo, anime/2D game art, and denoising. Use for any image resolution enhancement — '放大图片', 'upscale texture', 'enhance image quality', '提高分辨率'.
- **material-generator**: Generates PBR surface material assets (seamless PNG texture + Unity .mat file) in Unity using Huoshan SeeDream AI from text prompts, reference images, or material type presets
- **plan**: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.
- **search-assets**: Searches and downloads pre-made Unity assets from the cloud library, then places them in the scene. Use for '搜索资产', 'find a cat model', 'download a spaceship prefab', 'search the asset library for furniture', or any request to find/download existing Unity assets rather than generating new ones.
- **skybox-generator**: Generates Cubemap skybox assets in Unity using Rodin AI from text prompts or reference images, with automatic scene assignment via placeholder workflow
- **sprite-and-sprite-sequence-generator**: Handles ALL 2D sprite and sprite sequence tasks in Unity. Three modes — choose based on inputs: Mode A (Sprite only): user wants a static 2D sprite (icon, portrait, UI element, item image), no animation needed; Mode B (Sequence only): user wants a sprite sequence animation AND already has an existing image (image_path is provided); Mode C (Sprite → Sequence): user wants a sprite sequence animation but has NO existing image — generate the sprite first, wait for completion, then use the result as image_path for generate_sprite_sequence. Always use this agent for any combination of sprite and/or sprite sequence generation.
- **unity-insight**: Read-only Unity project analysis specialist (Unity Insight VFS). Use for prefab/scene hierarchy, script-to-asset usage, and Unity reference questions. When delegating via Task: state only what to find or answer (goals, scope, deliverables)—not how to investigate. Do not prescribe steps, workflows, search strategies, or tool names (e.g. vfs_ls, vfs_grep, vfs_read); this agent selects its own read-only VFS tools. For “which scene/prefab uses this .mat/model/texture” tasks, add one deliverable line: vfs_refs paths are sufficient evidence—do not require reading scene YAML or quoting m_Materials unless the user explicitly asks for field-level YAML. Optional thoroughness: quick | medium | very thorough.
